stories.title: Swinney says reform is at the heart of his programme for government
stories.summary: The first minister is due to set out his plans for the year ahead which are expected to include proposals for significant public service reform. John Swinney said it was time to "embrace change", with reforms to sit at the heart of his programme for government. He has already appointed a new cabinet minister to lead on public service reform and is also expected to set out a range of policies aimed at growing the economy, eradicating child poverty, transitioning to net zero and tackling violence against women and girls. Opposition parties have said they want to see further action on the NHS and cost of living. Swinney said he was committed to making sure Scotland delivered stronger economic growth, which he said would help tackle the challenges around child poverty and investment in public services. And he said he would be setting out measures to parliament that would address "the epidemic of violence against women and girls". Swinney is due to announce his programme for government to MSPs at the Scottish Parliament at 15:00. He said: "The government came into office with a commitment to deliver a 100-day programme, and the government is going to do exactly that. "And that's the first stage of me repaying the trust that the people of Scotland have put in my government, which is to deliver what I said to the public I would deliver." He said the government had to review the way it delivered public services. "We made clear before the election that was going to be necessary," he said. "I want to make sure that the programme for government reflects the ambitions I set out in my election manifesto, which was all about making sure that we tackle the cost of living challenges that people face in Scotland, that we deliver improvements in our public services."

stories.title: US ‘big enough’ to handle threats globally, vice president says
stories.summary: JD Vance commented on reports of weapons shortages affecting the US ability to respond to threats
article_sentences: NEW YORK, September 1.
Despite its conflict with Iran, Washington has sufficient capabilities to deal with threats around the world, US Vice President JD Vance said.

"We’re clearly big enough to handle threats around the world, including China." Vance told Fox News, when asked if he was concerned about reports of weapons shortages affecting the US ability to respond to threats.
He added that disagreements with China would not prevent Washington from seeking positive relations with Beijing.
"We recognize that they are a competitor.
We recognize they have the same ambitions that are going to conflict with ours, but we're also trying to have a positive relationship despite that," the US vice president noted.

stories.title: New storm names for 2026-2027 released by Met Office
stories.summary: The first of September marks the start of meteorological autumn, and with it the start of the UK's storm season. This year, expect to hear the names Austen, Boelo and Chloe, which are the first three on the alphabetical list, followed by Dano and Evelyn. Storms are named by the UK Met Office, Ireland's Met Éireann or the Netherlands' KNMI when they are forecast to cause "medium" or "high" impacts. Why are storms named? In the UK, storms are named when they are likely to cause disruption or damage that could lead to an amber or red warning being issued. This decision is based on both the potential impact of the weather and how likely it is to occur. Names are typically given to storms where impacts from strong winds are expected, although other weather-related effects are also taken into account such as heavy rainfall or snow which may lead to flooding or travel disruption. Using one official system to name storms helps to share clear and consistent information about severe weather, making it easier for the public to stay safe. The 2026-2027 marks the eleventh year of storm naming in the UK. How are storm names chosen? Storm names are selected jointly by the Met Office, Met Éireann and KNMI, with the final list aiming to reflect communities across the UK, Ireland and the Netherlands. In 2025 the three meteorology agencies invited nominations for names from the public.

stories.title: OPEC+ seven's quota rises by 188,000 bpd in September
stories.summary: The production quota reached 31.01 mln bpd
article_sentences: MOSCOW, September 1.

The oil production quota for the OPEC+ seven (Saudi Arabia, Russia, Iraq, Kuwait, Kazakhstan, Algeria and Oman) increases by 188,000 barrels per day (bpd) in September compared with August, to 31.01 mln bpd as the group completes the phaseout of its 1.65 mln bpd voluntary production cut, according to OPEC data and TASS calculations.

At their latest meeting, the seven leading OPEC+ countries decided to increase oil production by 188,000 bpd in September compared with August, bringing the group's oil production quota for the month to 31.01 mln bpd.

OPEC+ countries had also previously extended until the end of 2026 the period during which they can compensate for earlier overproduction, though an updated compensation schedule has yet to be published.
The previous schedule called for the compensation period to end in June 2026.

Starting in April 2025, the OPEC+ eight gradually began returning previously withheld barrels to the market, and in September 2025 the group fully unwound its voluntary production cuts of 2.2 mln bpd, a year ahead of the original schedule.
In October 2025, OPEC+ began gradually unwinding another oil production cut of 1.65 mln bpd.

Following the UAE's withdrawal from OPEC and OPEC+ on May 1, 2026, the group has operated as a seven-country format, with this production cut amounting to around 1.5 mln bpd excluding the UAE's share.

In September of this year, the OPEC+ seven will complete the phaseout of the voluntary oil production cut of 1.65 mln bpd, or 1.5 mln bpd excluding the quota of the UAE, which withdrew from OPEC and OPEC+ on May 1, fully returning the withheld volume to the market.
The OPEC+ seven will continue to hold monthly meetings to assess market conditions, with the next meeting scheduled for September 6.
